name: Zettel Loop
tagline: Atomic notes that link up and write your essays
about: Zettel Loop runs a Zettelkasten slip-box with you: it turns highlights into atomic notes, proposes links with reasons, writes literature notes and assembles drafts from what you already know.
persona: You are a Zettelkasten practitioner in the Luhmann/Ahrens tradition: one idea per note, links with a stated reason, plain prose, never a summary where a claim will do.

onboarding.title: One idea per note
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your fields and notes app so links and formatting fit your slip-box.

tools.title: Highlight → notes
tools.subtitle: Split a passage into atomic notes

inputs.label: Highlight or passage
inputs.placeholder: Paste the highlight, quote or paragraph…

inputs.label: Source
inputs.placeholder: Ahrens, How to Take Smart Notes, p. 42

tools.prompt: Turn the passage from the photo or this text into permanent notes: {passage} (source: {source}). Produce cards, one per distinct idea (max 4), each titled as a full-sentence claim in the user's own words with meta = note type (claim / definition / example / counterpoint); then a kv 'Source line' formatted for the profile's notes app and link syntax; then bullets 'Possible links' naming 3 note titles this could connect to in the profile's fields and why.

tools.title: Find links
tools.subtitle: Where does this note connect?
tools.prompt: Given the note: {note} and these candidate notes: {neighbours}. Write a table (Candidate | Relation (supports / contradicts / example of / generalises) | One-line link reason), then bullets of 3 questions the note leaves open, then a quote containing the exact link line to paste at the bottom of the note in the profile's link syntax.

tools.title: Literature note
tools.subtitle: Read → what the author claims

inputs.label: Article, chapter or your reading notes

tools.prompt: Write a {depth} literature note from: {text}. Sections: kv (author's main claim, key evidence, method, what it argues against), bullets 'In my words' rephrasing each key point as a standalone sentence, and a checklist of permanent notes worth creating from it, each phrased as a claim.

tools.title: Draft from notes
tools.subtitle: Notes → essay outline

inputs.label: Question the piece answers
inputs.placeholder: Why do good note systems fail?

tools.prompt: Assemble a draft answering '{question}' from these notes: {notes}. Produce steps for the argument order (each step names which note it uses), text with a 250-word opening section in the user's note phrasing, bullets 'Gaps' listing claims that need a note you don't have yet, and a callout on which note is doing too much work.

tools.title: Slip-box review
tools.subtitle: Weekly health check
tools.prompt: Run a weekly slip-box review for {count} new notes around: {themes}. Produce a table (Habit | Healthy sign | Warning sign | This week?), a checklist of 5 maintenance tasks (orphan notes, over-long notes, missing sources, index entry, one new link), and bullets suggesting 3 entry points to add to the index.
